D000069.s: Process of cultural change in which one group or members of a group assimilate various cultural patterns from another.

D001365.s: Area of the human body underneath the shoulder joint, also known as the armpit or underarm.

D001835.s: The mass or quantity of heaviness of an individual. It is expressed by units of pounds or kilograms.

D002386.s: Partial or complete opacity on or in the lens or capsule of one or both eyes, impairing vision or causing blindness. The many kinds of cataract are classified by their morphology (size, shape, location) or etiology (cause and time of occurrence). (Dorland, 27th ed)

D002650.s: Sexual maltreatment of the child or minor.

D003095.s: Historically, a heterogeneous group of acute and chronic diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, progressive systemic sclerosis, dermatomyositis, etc.

D003433.s: Deliberate breeding of two different individuals that results in offspring that carry part of the genetic material of each parent. The parent organisms must be genetically compatible and may be from different varieties or closely related species.

D003446.s: Wooden or metal staffs designed to aid a person in walking. (umdns,1999)

D003925.s: Vascular diseases that are associated with diabetes mellitus.

D004595.s: Coating with a metal or alloy by electrolysis.

D005655.s: Those customs and ceremonies pertaining to the dead.

D006179.s: One of the convolutions on the medial surface of the cerebral hemispheres. It surrounds the rostral part of the brain and corpus callosum and forms part of the limbic system.

D006294.s: Destinations frequented as vacation or recreational retreats, equipped with specialized amenities, treatments and facilities, for the promotion of general well-being and health.

D007345.s: Review of claims by insurance companies to determine liability and amount of payment for various services.

D007415.s: Any impairment, arrest, or reversal of the normal flow of intestinal contents toward the anal canal.

D008465.s: Cells specialized to transduce mechanical stimuli and relay that information centrally in the nervous system. Mechanoreceptor cells include the inner ear hair cells, which mediate hearing and balance, and the various somatosensory receptors, often with non-neural accessory structures.

D009000.s: Large, phagocytic mononuclear leukocytes produced in the vertebrate bone marrow and released into the blood; contain a large, oval or somewhat indented nucleus surrounded by voluminous cytoplasm and numerous organelles.

D009736.s: The sum total of nursing activities which includes assessment (identifying needs), intervention (ministering to needs), and evaluation (validating the effectiveness of the help given).

D009743.s: The practice of nursing by licensed, non-registered persons qualified to provide routine care to the sick.

D009817.s: Planning, organizing, and administering activities in an office.

D011489.s: Disruption of the non-covalent bonds and/or disulfide bonds responsible for maintaining the three-dimensional shape and activity of the native protein.

D012516.s: A sarcoma originating in bone-forming cells, affecting the ends of long bones. It is the most common and most malignant of sarcomas of the bones, and occurs chiefly among 10- to 25-year-old youths. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

D012563.s: A chronic form of schizophrenia characterized primarily by the presence of persecutory or grandiose delusions, often associated with hallucination.

D012945.s: Abstract standards or empirical variables in social life which are believed to be important and/or desirable.

D013010.s: The application of high intensity ultrasound to liquids.

D013164.s: Anastomosis of splenic vein to renal vein to relieve portal hypertension.

D013568.s: Abnormal anatomical or physiological conditions and objective or subjective manifestations of disease, not classified as disease or syndrome.

D013681.s: Portion of midbrain situated under the dorsal tectum mesencephali. The two ventrolateral cylindrical masses or peduncles are large nerve fiber bundles providing a tract of passage between the forebrain with the hindbrain.

D014147.s: A narcotic analgesic proposed for severe pain. It may be habituating.

D014392.s: Tuberculous infection of the eye, primarily the iris, ciliary body, and choroid.

D015009.s: Infections with bacteria of the genus yersinia.

D015452.s: A leukemia/lymphoma found predominately in children and adolescents and characterized by a high number of lymphoblasts and solid tumor lesions. Frequent sites involve lymph nodes, skin, and bones. It most commonly presents as leukemia.

D016057.s: Electrical waves in the cerebral cortex generated by brain stem structures in response to auditory click stimuli. These are found to be abnormal in many patients with cerebellopontine angle lesions, multiple sclerosis, or other demyelinating diseases.

D016251.s: An optical disk storage system for computers on which data can be read or from which data can be retrieved but not entered or modified. A CD-ROM unit is almost identical to the compact disk playback device for home use.

D016390.s: Occupations of medical personnel who are not physicians, and are qualified by special training and, frequently, by licensure to work in supporting roles in the health care field. These occupations include, but are not limited to, medical technology, physical therapy, physician assistant, etc.

D016501.s: In tissue culture, hairlike projections of neurons stimulated by growth factors and other molecules. These projections may go on to form a branched tree of dendrites or a single axon or they may be reabsorbed at a later stage of development.

D017119.s: An autosomal dominant or acquired porphyria due to a deficiency of uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase in the liver. It is characterized by photosensitivity and cutaneous lesions with little or no neurologic symptoms.

D017542.s: The tearing or bursting of the weakened wall of the aneurysmal sac, usually heralded by sudden worsening pain. The great danger of a ruptured aneurysm is the large amount of blood spilling into the surrounding tissues and cavities, causing hemorrhagic shock.

D018154.s: Created 1 January 1993 as a result of the division of Czechoslovakia into the Czech Republic and Slovakia.

D018240.s: An unusual and aggressive tumor of germ-cell origin that reproduces the extraembryonic structures of the early embryo. It is the most common malignant germ cell tumor found in children.

D018327.s: A cellular subtype of malignant melanoma. It is a pigmented lesion composed of melanocytes occurring on sun-exposed skin, usually the face and neck. The melanocytes are commonly multinucleated with a starburst appearance. It is considered by many to be the in situ phase of lentigo maligna melanoma.

e: Congenital Fissure of the Abdominal Cavity
D020139.s: A congenital defect with major fissure in the abdominal wall lateral to, but not at, the umbilicus. This results in the extrusion of viscera. Unlike omphalocele, herniated structures in gastroschisis are not covered by a sac or peritoneum.

D021521.s: Restriction fragment length polymorphism analysis of rRNA genes that is used for differentiating between species or strains.

D032882.s: The act or fact of grasping the meaning, nature, or importance of; understanding. (American Heritage Dictionary, 4th ed) Includes understanding by a patient or research subject of information disclosed orally or in writing.

D044708.s: Head to tail array of covalently joined DNA sequences generated by concatenation. Concatenated DNA is attached end to end in contrast to catenated dna which is attached loop to loop.

D047688.s: A fluid-filled closed cavity or sac that is lined by an epithelium and found in the breast. It may appear as a single large cyst in one breast, multifocal, or bilateral in fibrocystic breast disease.

D050507.s: Fatty tissue under the SKIN in the region of the abdomen.

D053803.s: The application of genetic analyses and molecular diagnostic techniques to legal matters and crime analysis.

D054626.s: Information intended for potential users of medical and healthcare services. There is an emphasis on self-care and preventive approaches as well as information for community-wide dissemination and use.

D055113.s: Chronic inflammation and loss of periodontium that is associated with the amount of dental plaque or dental calculus present. Chronic periodontitis occurs mostly in adults and was called adult periodontitis, but this disease can appear in young people.

D055166.s: Perisinusoidal cells of the liver, located in the space of Disse between hepatocytes and sinusoidal endothelial cells.

D055948.s: Progressive decline in muscle mass due to aging which results in decreased functional capacity of muscles.

D057128.s: The use of an aberrometer to measure eye tissue imperfections or abnormalities based on the way light passes through the eye which affects the ability of the eye to focus properly.

D057898.s: An individual having only one allele at a given locus because of the loss of the other allele through a mutation (e.g., chromosome deletion).

D057906.s: Biological mechanism that controls circadian rhythm. Circadian clocks exist in the simplest form in cyanobacteria and as more complex systems in fungi, plants, and animals.

D057973.s: X-linked recessive nephrolithiasis characterized by hypercalciuria; hypophosphatemia; nephrocalcinosis; and proteinuria. It is associated with mutations in the voltage-gated chloride channel, CLC-5 (Dent Disease I).

D058536.s: Dilation of fetal kidney pelvis. It is a common prenatal ultrasonography finding with no significant long-term sequelae.

D058891.s: Drugs that inhibit 3-OXO-5-alpha-steroid 4-dehydrogenase. They are commonly used to reduce the production of dihydrotestosterone.

D061147.s: The treatment of immune system diseases by deliberate infestation with helminths. This therapy is partly based on the hygiene hypothesis which states that the absence of parasites increases immune dysregulation because of the lack of stimulation of regulatory T-cells.

D066296.s: The generation of theories from analysis of empirical data.

D000070297.s: Physical resistance to motion between dental surfaces.

D000070356.s: Persons skilled and/or qualified to operate an aircraft or ship.

D000070598.s: Sprain or tear injuries to the anterior cruciate ligament of the knee.

D000071081.s: A statistically significant minimum set of clinical outcomes that demonstrates a clinical benefit of an intervention or treatment.

D000074222.s: Obsessive thinking about an idea, situation, or choice.

D000075782.s: Utilization of wireless phones for communication.

D000081015.s: Damage to the EAR or its function secondary to exposure to toxic substances such as drugs used in chemotherapy; immunotherapy; or radiation.

D000087602.s: Environmental alterations resulting from human activities.

D000090242.s: Testing administered with level of difficulty l is tailored to the test taker.

D000091902.s: The ability of a plant to adapt in a drought environment and tolerate a reduction in available water.

D000099111.s: Tests in which two tasks are performed simultaneously. Dual-Task Exercises can be used to show the performance differences of subjects in multitasking behavior.
